clue.text: Piece of Holst to which Tom Towers contributed

definitions.meaning: a movement of Holst's suite The Planets, named after the largest planet
Tom Towers is the journalist in Trollope's novel The Warden who writes for a newspaper of this name

explanation.surface: A music quiz question about which Holst piece a certain Tom Towers had a hand in.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Towers looks like a composer or performer, but he is a fictional journalist from Trollope's Barchester novels, whose paper is a thinly veiled version of The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's orchestral suite The Planets has a movement named after the Roman king of the gods, and Trollope's newspaper bears the same name.

clue.text: Just a crow kind, dark and whiter on top

definitions.text: Just a crow kind, dark and whiter on top

parts.words: Just a crow kind, dark and whiter on top
parts.note: a small member of the crow family, black overall with a pale grey nape and pale eye

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note on a dark crow-like bird with a paler head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the bird: a small black crow with a greyish back of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small crow, black with a grey nape, so it matches the description.

clue.text: What may be used by pushers in a fix?

definitions.text: What may be used by pushers in a fix?

parts.words: What may be used by pushers in a fix?
parts.note: a switch pressed by people in an emergency to raise the alarm; pushers are those who push it, a fix a predicament

explanation.surface: A question about what drug dealers might use when supplying a dose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushers' and 'fix' suggest drug dealers and doses; really they are people pressing a button when in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the alarm switch pressed in an emergency, so people in a fix push it.

clue.text: Act foolishly and start to toy with gun

indicators.note: the start of the next word means its first letter

parts.note: a rifle is a type of gun

explanation.surface: Someone behaves stupidly and begins to play with a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to behave frivolously or treat something without due seriousness.

clue.text: Paparazzo going after sunburnt swimmer

indicators.note: the paparazzo is placed after the other word

parts.note: sunburnt skin is red
a snapper is a photographer, especially a press one

explanation.surface: A celebrity photographer chases a sunburnt person bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer is a fish, a crossword convention; a paparazzo is a press photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper is a reddish food fish, and fish are crossword swimmers.

clue.text: Silly person denied love left with daughter and betrayed husband

indicators.note: the silly person is refused one of its letters, so something is taken away from that word

parts.note: a cuckoo is a slang term for a fool or crazy person
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A fool who has lost love, together with a daughter, ends up as a husband deceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly person' tempts one to look for an anagram signal, but it is a synonym that loses one letter for love.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose wife is unfaithful is traditionally called by this old word, so a betrayed husband fits exactly.

clue.text: Prepare to swallow cold chop

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to hew is to chop, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Getting a cold pork chop ready to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing food is what you do to make it ready for swallowing.

clue.text: Working in service, he does treble duty

definitions.text: Working in service, he does treble duty

parts.words: Working in service, he does treble duty
parts.note: a boy who sings in church services, taking the treble line, the highest voice part

explanation.surface: A servant who has to perform three jobs at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treble duty' suggests three jobs, and 'service' domestic work; really it is a church service and the high treble voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy singer in a church choir sings the treble part during services.

clue.text: Blade of grass cut by mower at last

indicators.note: the grass is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: oat is a cereal grass

indicators.note: the last letter of the mower is taken

explanation.surface: A single blade of grass trimmed by a lawnmower in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks OAT to OA, and 'at last' takes R from mower. The rowing blade is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar is called its blade, and the word can stand for the whole oar.

clue.text: Act to confine swan in part of pool

indicators.note: one word encloses the other, keeping it inside

parts.note: a deed is an act
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Legislation passed to keep a swan in one section of a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swan' gives a female swan, a word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep end is the part of a swimming pool with the greatest depth.

clue.text: Learn to direct trick against prisoner

definitions.meaning: to study or memorise something carefully, an old verb sense
to steer a ship, giving orders to the helmsman
the opposite side of an argument

explanation.surface: Someone learns how to pull off a trick against a jailed man.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word or phrase here is a separate definition of the same three-letter word, so it is a multiple definition rather than a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word has many senses: study, steer a vessel, swindle, an argument against, and a convict.

clue.text: Hunt expected to arrive in reverse order or in the natural order

indicators.note: the three pieces are listed in the clue back to front, so they are assembled the other way round

parts.note: a train due is expected to arrive
to course is to hunt hares with hounds

explanation.surface: A hunt party is expected to arrive, either in reverse order or in the usual sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives Hunt, expected to arrive, in; 'reverse order' says to put them down last-first: IN, DUE, COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at the proper or expected time, when things happen in their natural sequence.

clue.text: Avoid fish and a little fowl

parts.note: to duck a question is to avoid it
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge the fish course and a small bird dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A young duck is a small bird of the poultry kind, so a little fowl describes it.

clue.text: What often holds up window cleaners on a big task

definitions.text: What often holds up window cleaners on a big task

parts.words: What often holds up window cleaners on a big task
parts.note: the platform slung by ropes down the face of a tall building, in which workers stand to clean its windows

explanation.surface: A question about what delays window cleaners when the job is large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' suggests delays, but here it is literal: the thing physically supports the cleaners high on a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspended platform lowered down a building's face to carry window cleaners or painters bears this name.

clue.text: As little chap's going under, medic leading operation seen to be clumsy with needle

indicators.note: the medic goes in front of the next piece
in a down clue, these pieces sit below the others

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
taken as written
titch is a nickname for a small person

explanation.surface: A small man goes under anaesthetic while a doctor operates clumsily with a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'going under' means the little chap's part comes below the medic and operation. Titch is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a stitch is to let a loop slip off the needle when knitting, a clumsy mistake.

clue.text: University tolerates awfully lazy person

indicators.note: done awfully, so the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A college puts up with someone terribly idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges U with TOLERATES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, eaters of the lotus fruit lose all ambition, so the name means an idle dreamer.

clue.text: During short stroll, you heard cry like cat

indicators.note: one piece sits within the time of another, so it goes inside it
the stroll is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: to walk is to stroll

indicators.note: the word you is said aloud, sounding like a single letter

parts.note: spoken, the word sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: While out on a brief walk, you heard a feline yowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims WALK to WAL; 'heard' turns 'you' into U; 'During' puts U inside WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To waul (or wawl) is a dialect verb for the wailing cry of a cat, as in caterwaul.

clue.text: Making mischief? No more than useless

parts.note: as many as, but not exceeding, as in up to ten
something that is no good is useless

explanation.surface: Someone causing trouble is nothing more than a waste of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up to no good is engaged in mischief or plotting wrongdoing, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: Lasting record of UN rising in importance

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: moment means importance, as in a matter of great moment

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A permanent memorial of the United Nations growing in significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importance' gives a less familiar sense: a matter of great moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a structure or record that preserves a memory over time.

clue.text: Silent, although made more emphatic

parts.note: but can mean although, introducing a contrast
toned up means strengthened or intensified

explanation.surface: Someone says nothing, even though their manner has become more forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being buttoned up is an idiom for tight-lipped and reticent, saying little.

clue.text: Shock follows what one may do to cat in lab equipment

indicators.note: the shock comes after the other piece

parts.words: what one may do to cat
parts.note: to bell the cat, from the fable, is to hang a bell on it
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A jolt comes after something done to a cat in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: Belling the cat comes from the fable in which mice plan to hang a bell on a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a bell-shaped glass cover used in laboratories.

clue.text: Fine and cool? Just the reverse

definitions.text: Fine and cool? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the pieces are to be read backwards to give the answer

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a fan is a device used to cool a room

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is classy and stylish and is told it is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' is an adjective on the surface but here the noun FAN; 'Just the reverse' turns F + FAN backwards, and also says the answer is the opposite of fine and cool.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tacky or unfashionable, the opposite of fine and cool, so the whole clue defines it.

clue.text: Sack over small computer error? It's flaming criminal

indicators.note: in a down clue, the sack sits above the other piece

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
a bug is a fault in a program

explanation.surface: Dismissal over a minor software glitch is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaming' sounds like a mild oath, but it literally describes the arsonist.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebug is an arsonist, a criminal who sets things ablaze.

clue.text: Trouble held up plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
had means held or possessed

explanation.surface: A flower is delayed by a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIL + HAD backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant with showy flowers.

clue.text: Monkey showing fatigue without oxygen

indicators.note: the fatigue loses something, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: languor is weariness or lassitude
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An ape displays tiredness through lack of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes an O from LANGOUR, the British spelling of languor.
explanation.definitionFit: A langur is a long-tailed Asian leaf monkey.

clue.text: Discourage holding tin or glass full of drink

indicators.note: one word is placed around the other, as if holding it

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone discourages using a tin, preferring a glass of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is just a link; the definition is a whole phrase for the glass vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel from which wine or spirits are served.

clue.text: Look up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up the grid as going down, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Glance upwards and downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: read up or down it is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick look.

clue.text: Critical Hardy hero comes across good and crazy

indicators.note: the hero stretches across the letter, so it goes inside him

parts.note: Jude Fawley is the hero of Thomas Hardy's novel Jude the Obscure
mental is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A disapproving Hardy protagonist meets someone good and wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy's hero is from Jude the Obscure; 'comes across' means he spans the letter for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Judgemental means quick to criticise others, so critical is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pair proudly taken up to centre

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, backwards
only the central letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A couple proudly carried up to the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to centre' takes OUD from the middle of 'proudly' and 'taken up' turns it to DUO.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, especially of performers.

clue.text: Container that's usually round, however turned

indicators.note: the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: but can mean however

explanation.surface: A rounded vessel, yet one that has been flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' runs BUT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a wide container, typically circular, for washing or storage.

clue.text: Part of house to proof in a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws the letters about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A section of the house that needs weatherproofing during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges the letters of 'to proof'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooftop is the uppermost outer part of a house.

clue.text: Go hard all over the place, let nothing in — this driver?

indicators.note: the nothing is let in, placed inside the rearranged letters
letters scattered everywhere, so rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Drive hard, swerving everywhere and letting no one in: describing a selfish motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges GO HARD; 'let ... in' puts O (nothing) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a selfish motorist who hogs the road and won't let others in.
